title: Microsoft Teams: events registration capacity rises to 20,000
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft's planned limits, rollout windows, licensing requirements and documented controls are accurately reported. One minor correction remains: the checklist instructs readers to review the event inventory, but that monitoring control is not represented in the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Teams events registration capacity of up to 20,000 for organisers with valid attendee packs.
claims.quote: Connect with more attendees than ever before with Teams Events, now supporting up to 20,000 registrations for organizers with valid Attendee packs.

claims.claim: Registration capacity scales with the event's attendee capacity, subject to the 20,000-registration maximum.
claims.quote: Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.

claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise ... Attendee packs enable organizers to host events beyond the 3,000-attendee limit.

claims.claim: The Learn pack pages do not publish a price for Attendee Capacity Packs.

claims.claim: A charge specific to registration above 3,000 is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack price registration charge 3000 20000. Read MC1557760, both pack pages, feature comparison and events-licensing search excerpts; no registration-specific charge or meter is stated.

claims.claim: Managing pack assignments in the Teams admin center requires the Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrators have read-only access to the Teams admin center License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.claim: Removing an assigned pack may leave upcoming events ineligible to run at their originally scheduled capacity.
claims.quote: If an attendee pack is removed after an event is scheduled, the upcoming event might no longer be eligible to run at the originally scheduled capacity.

claims.claim: Teams notifies the administrator of the potential impact of removing a pack.
claims.quote: To reduce the risk of event disruption, Teams notifies both the admin and the organizer.

claims.claim: Teams notifies the organiser when their pack is removed.
claims.quote: The organizer receives an email notification that informs them the attendee pack was removed with a list of affected events.

claims.claim: Organisers use a unified creation flow to configure settings such as registration based on event capacity and scenario.
claims.quote: Organizers use a unified creation flow to configure event settings—such as registration and attendee interaction—based on event capacity and scenario, rather than selecting a fixed event type.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for the registration-capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events registration capacity 20000 data compliance autonomous policy webinars registration 1000. Read MC1557760 and relevant creation-flow and registration passages in Plan for Teams events; none describes autonomous behaviour for this increase.

claims.claim: No change to data access or data destination is documented for this registration-capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events registration capacity 20000 data compliance autonomous policy webinars registration 1000. Read MC1557760, pack pages, and relevant Plan for Teams events passages; no new data access or destination is stated for the increase.

claims.claim: MC1557760 identifies no compliance considerations.

claims.claim: Pack assignment is at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. ... On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users ... In the Assign Add-on licenses pane ... select the pack size that you want to assign in the Attendee pack column.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense assigns or removes purchased user licences, providing automation for pack assignment.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body uses addLicenses to specify licences to add.
claims.quote: addLicenses ... A collection of assignedLicense objects that specify the licenses to add.

claims.claim: removeLicenses identifies licences to remove by SKU ID.
claims.quote: removeLicenses ... A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: The webinar creation setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled permits organisers under that policy to create events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: AllowWebinars is the existing control for creating events up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars.
claims.quote: Events up to 1k attendees ... -AllowWebinars ... Controls whether users with this policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars.

claims.claim: The large-audience creation setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled permits organisers under that policy to create events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled

claims.where: controls[2].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: AllowTownhalls controls creation of events optimised for large audiences, such as town halls.
claims.quote: Events optimized for a large audience ... -AllowTownhalls ... Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Town hall attendee access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone allows any user to attend large-audience events created under that policy.
claims.quote: To allow any user to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone

claims.claim: The matching attendee-access parameter for events up to 1,000 attendees is EventAccessType.
claims.quote: For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, use the -EventAccessType parameter.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels the policy as preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The management guide presents the listed event policy controls without a preview label.
claims.quote: Searched: preview in the full fetched Manage who can schedule and attend events in Microsoft Teams guide. Read its overview, scheduling and attendance sections; no preview label appears, unlike the cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: MC1557760 does not identify which existing toggle governs a webinar with more than 1,000 registrations.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events registration capacity 20000 data compliance autonomous policy webinars registration 1000. Read MC1557760 in full; it requires the right events policy but names no toggle for webinars above 1,000 registrations.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center Teams Events page shows purchased pack stock and current assignments.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Teams Events page, you see your organization's attendee pack inventory, including available attendee packs that you purchased and current assignments.

claims.claim: The event inventory lets administrators review events affected by removing an organiser's pack.
claims.quote: When an admin removes an attendee pack from an organizer who has upcoming events: ... In the event inventory, admins can view the list of affected events.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to review the event inventory without a corresponding monitoring row in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review the event inventory before removing or changing a pack ... Table rows: Attendee Capacity Pack assignment; webinar creation; large-audience event creation; town hall attendee access.
claims.fix: Replace the After rollout bullet 'Review the event inventory before removing or changing a pack, because Learn warns upcoming events may no longer run at the scheduled capacity' with 'Consider the impact before removing or changing a pack, because Learn warns upcoming events may no longer run at the scheduled capacity.' This removes the inventory-control instruction that has no table row without adding a row.
